entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Claude recommended an Always-On Sandbox because the team needs immediate shared access for read-only API practice without waiting for provisioning.
entries.rationale: The official Sandbox documentation confirms Always-On environments are shared and available instantly for API exploration, but restrict administrative privileges, which matches this read-only, no-wait use case exactly.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Claude recommended a Reservation Sandbox because the team needs private, administrative access to test configuration changes and can accept setup and VPN time.
entries.rationale: The Sandbox FAQ confirms reservation sandboxes are private with full administrative access, but the AI understated that setup normally takes fifteen to forty-five minutes, so I added that constraint to the rationale.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Claude recommended a DevNet Learning Lab because the beginner needs guided, step-by-step instruction before attempting an independent API activity.
entries.rationale: The DevNet Learning site describes self-paced, hands-on tutorials designed to teach API concepts before independent practice, which fits a beginner who needs structured guidance rather than an execution environment.

entries.ai_recommendation_summary: Claude recommended Cisco Code Exchange because the developer wants to review existing community and Cisco-maintained automation repositories before building a new solution.
entries.rationale: The AI first referred to this resource as Automation Exchange, but the official page confirms Automation Exchange was consolidated into Code Exchange, so I corrected the label to match current Cisco terminology.
